caption:
Marriage didn’t slow your metabolism.
Comfort slowed your discipline.
After marriage, priorities change, workouts become “kal se”, food becomes emotional, health becomes optional.
Then weight goes up… and metabolism becomes the scapegoat.
Studies are clear:
👉 metabolism doesn’t suddenly crash
👉 habits do
👉 mindset does
Marriage settles your life, not your body fat goals.
That part still needs effort.
Stop blaming biology for lifestyle choices.

transcript.text: Why do people suddenly get fat after marriage? [Original HI: Yeh shaadi ke baad log achanak mote kyu ho jate hain?]
The science behind this is a little uncomfortable.
Even though most people think it's because you're entering your thirties and your metabolism has slowed down,
a long-term study followed more than 6,000 people
from their early 20s to almost 60,
and shockingly, it showed that their metabolism barely changed.
So neither your age nor your marriage killed your metabolism. [Original HI: Toh na tumhari umar aur na tumhari shaadi ne tumhara metabolism kill kiya hai.]
What changed was your behavior.
See, your priorities shift after marriage.
Career, family, stability, comfort.
And slowly and silently the self-neglect starts.
Who cares about the body, [Original HI: Body bhaad mein jaaye,]
overeating becomes normal and life becomes sedentary.
More than half of people run to coaches
months before marriage saying 'I need urgent fat loss.' [Original HI: urgent fat loss chahiye.]
How many people have you seen saying this after marriage?
The deadline disappears, so does discipline.
So it's not a biological problem,
it's a psychological problem.
So stop looking for things to blame.
You got married, you didn't win an Oscar. [Original HI: Shaadi hui hai, koi Oscar nahi jeeta hai tumne.]
Instead of retiring from your own health at 30,
it's an opportunity to reshape your lifestyle.
And this time you won't have to do it all alone.
And if you need help doing that,
DM UNLOCK to start your fitness journey today.

hook.template: Why do people suddenly [CHANGE] after [LIFE EVENT]? The science behind this is a little uncomfortable.
hook.whyItWorks: Weight gain after marriage is something nearly every Indian viewer has seen in a cousin, a friend or the mirror, so the Hinglish question lands instantly. 'A little uncomfortable' warns that the answer will point at the viewer, which makes them stay to see if it's about them. Her scrunched, sceptical face sells the tone before the words do.

format.visualLayout: Single seated talking head at home holding a mic windscreen, chunked white captions in the centre, one research-paper screenshot overlay
format.pacing: medium: one location, jump cuts about every 2 to 3s, no b-roll except a 5s study overlay
format.reasoning: A blunt opinion works best face to face: no graphics to hide behind, just her expressions and a few punchlines in Hindi. The study screenshot appears exactly when she makes the science claim, then disappears so the focus returns to her.

angle.commonBelief: Marriage and turning 30 slow your metabolism, so weight gain is natural
angle.contrarianTake: Priorities shift, workouts stop and the wedding deadline is gone; it's a behaviour problem, and fixable

myVersion.hook: Got married, gained eight kilos, and now everyone says 'it's normal after shaadi'? Let's talk about that.
myVersion.script:
Got married, gained eight kilos, and now everyone says 'it's normal after shaadi'? Let's talk about that.
I hear this from so many women who join my program.
And when we actually sit down and look at their day, the story is always the same.
Before the wedding, there was a date on the calendar. Lehenga fittings. Photos. You were walking, eating clean, maybe even lifting.
After the wedding? New house, new kitchen, new routine.
You're cooking for everyone. You eat what's left on the plate so nothing goes waste.
Dinner moves to ten thirty because that's when the family eats.
Every weekend there's a function, a dawat, a relative's house.
And your workout? It became 'from Monday.' Every Monday.
None of this is your fault. But none of it is your body's fault either.
So before you blame your hormones or your age, look at what actually changed.
Your sleep. Your steps. Your portions. Your time for yourself.
That's good news, because habits can be changed. Starting this week.
Pick one thing. A twenty-minute walk after dinner. Or eating your own plate first instead of the leftovers.
Small, boring, repeatable.
Your shaadi was a celebration. It wasn't the end of your fitness.
Want help building your routine around your new life? DM me ROUTINE.
